title: Discovery of a mutant-selective covalent inhibitor of EGFR that overcomes T790M-mediated resistance in NSCLC.
abstract: Patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with activating EGF receptor (EGFR) mutations initially respond to first-generation reversible EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors.
However, clinical efficacy is limited by acquired resistance, frequently driven by the EGFR(T790M) mutation.

CO-1686 is a novel, irreversible, and orally delivered kinase inhibitor that specifically targets the mutant forms of EGFR, including T790M, while exhibiting minimal activity toward the wild-type (WT) receptor.
Oral administration of CO-1686 as single agent induces tumor regression in EGFR-mutated NSCLC tumor xenograft and transgenic models.
Minimal activity of CO-1686 against the WT EGFR receptor was observed.

In NSCLC cells with acquired resistance to CO-1686 in vitro, there was no evidence of additional mutations or amplification of the EGFR gene, but resistant cells exhibited signs of epithelial-mesenchymal transition and demonstrated increased sensitivity to AKT inhibitors.
These results suggest that CO-1686 may offer a novel therapeutic option for patients with mutant EGFR NSCLC.

We report the preclinical development of a novel covalent inhibitor, CO-1686, that irreversibly and selectively inhibits mutant EGFR, in particular the T790M drug-resistance mutation, in NSCLC models.

CO-1686 is the fi rst drug of its class in clinical development for the treatment of T790M-positive NSCLC, potentially offering potent inhibition of mutant EGFR while avoiding the on-target toxicity observed with inhibition of the WT EGFR.

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: Despite years of research and prevention strategies, lung cancer remains the most common cancer worldwide with approximately 1.35 million new cases annually.

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounts for almost 85% of all lung cancers ().

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: Additionally, lung cancer continues to be the most common cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide with a 5-year survival rate of less than 20% in patients in the US (http://seer.cancer.gov).

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: Activating mutations in the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) are key drivers of NSCLC malignancy in 10-15% of patients of European descent and approximately 30% of patients of East Asian descent ().

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: Patients with the most common EGFR mutations (L858R mutation in exon 21 and delE746-A750 deletions in exon 19) typically have good responses to therapy with first-generation reversible EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), such as erlotinib or gefitinib (-).

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: Toxicity associated with both erlotinib and gefitinib includes skin rash and diarrhea related to inhibition of wild-type EGFR (WT EGFR) in skin and intestine, respectively ().

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: Despite the impressive initial response to treatment, disease progression generally occurs after 9 to 14 months of erlotinib or gefitinib therapy, driven in approximately 60% of cases by a second site EGFR point mutation that results in the substitution of threonine with methionine at amino acid position 790 (T790M;(-)).

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: Research suggests that T790M mediates resistance to first-generation EGFR inhibitors by acting as a “gatekeeper” mutation, inducing steric hindrance in the ATP-binding pocket and preventing inhibitor binding (, , ).

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: Additional work has indicated that T790M increases the affinity of EGFR for ATP, therefore out-competing ATP-competitive TKIs and restoring enzymatic activity in their presence ().

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: Patients with mutant EGFR NSCLC who have failed treatment with first generation EGFR TKIs and have acquired resistance through the T790M mutation have few treatment options.

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: There are no targeted therapies for these patients, who are currently treated with cytotoxic chemotherapy that has limited efficacy, but significant toxicity, in the second- or third-line setting.

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: Although second generation irreversible HER-family TKIs, including dacomitinib (PF299804) and afatinib (BIBW2992), are able to inhibit T790M-mutant EGFR in vitro, in clinical trials these agents have not been shown to induce compelling responses in patients that have failed first-generation TKIs ().

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: Likely due to the potent inhibition of WT EGFR and its consequent toxicities, these agents cannot reach exposures in the clinic required to inhibit T790M in tumor tissue.

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: To circumvent this problem, a covalent inhibitor that inhibits mutant EGFR, including T790M, more potently than the WT receptor, termed WZ4002, was described (), but did not progress into human clinical trials.

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: Recently PKC-412 (midostaurin), an indolocarbazole compound currently in development as a FLT-3 inhibitor in acute myeloid leukemia, was described to selectively inhibit T790M over WT EGFR in a non-covalent fashion ().

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: As a staurosporine-derived compound, PKC412 has a broad kinase inhibition profile () and its clinical application in T790M positive NSCLC is therefore questionable, particularly since it doesn't potently inhibit activating EGFR mutations.

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: Hence, there is currently a need for an EGFR-TKI that is able to effectively treat T790M-positive lung tumors.

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: In the current study, we report the preclinical validation of a 2,4-disubstituted pyrimidine compound, CO-1686, that irreversibly and selectively inhibits mutant EGFR, in particular the T790M drug-resistance mutation, in NSCLC models.

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: Oral administration of CO-1686 leads to tumor regressions in cell-based and patient-derived xenograft models as well as in a transgenic mouse model expressing mutant forms of human EGFR.

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: In these models, acquired resistance to this third generation EGFR TKI is not mediated by further second-site mutations or amplification of the EGFR gene and resistant cells appear to have a reduced dependence on EGFR signaling compared to parental cells.

body.section: INTRODUCTION
body.text: CO-1686 is currently being evaluated in phase I/II clinical trials in EGFR-mutant NSCLC.

body.section: CO-1686 is a potent and irreversible inhibitor of EGFR in vitro
body.text: Using a structure-based approach, we designed and developed a potent 2,4-disubstituted pyrimidine molecule, CO-1686, that covalently modified the conserved Cys797 in the ATP binding pocket of the EGFR kinase domain (Fig. 1A).

body.section: CO-1686 is a potent and irreversible inhibitor of EGFR in vitro
body.text: As shown in the structural model of CO-1686 in complex with EGFR T790M, the meta acrylamide points to Cys797 and forms the covalent bond (Fig. 1B).

body.section: CO-1686 is a potent and irreversible inhibitor of EGFR in vitro
body.text: To confirm that CO-1686 covalently modified the EGFR L858R/T790M kinase we performed mass spectrometry.

body.section: CO-1686 is a potent and irreversible inhibitor of EGFR in vitro
body.text: Incubation of CO-1686 with recombinant EGFR L858R/T790M protein resulted in a mass shift of EGFR L858R/T790M consistent with the formation of a covalent complex between CO-1686 and the EGFR L858R/T790M protein (SI Fig. 1A).

body.section: CO-1686 is a potent and irreversible inhibitor of EGFR in vitro
body.text: Pepsin digest analyses confirmed that CO-1686 modified the conserved Cys797 residue in the EGFR L858R/T790M kinase domain (SI Fig. 1B, C).

body.section: CO-1686 is a potent and irreversible inhibitor of EGFR in vitro
body.text: To determine the selectivity and potency of CO-1686 in vitro we performed kinetic studies using recombinant WT EGFR and mutant EGFR L858R/T790M kinases.

body.section: CO-1686 is a potent and irreversible inhibitor of EGFR in vitro
body.text: When assessing a covalent inhibitor like CO-1686, potency is expressed by using the ratio (kinact/Ki) of the inactivation rate constant (kinact) with respect to the binding constant (Ki) since the amount of active EGFR enzyme changes over time.

body.section: CO-1686 is a potent and irreversible inhibitor of EGFR in vitro
body.text: CO-1686 is a potent inhibitor of EGFR L858R/T790M kinase (kinact/Ki = (2.41 ± 0.30) × 105 M-1s-1) and is approximately 22-fold selective over WT EGFR (kinactt/Ki = (1.12 ± 0.14) × 104 M-1s-1) (Table 1).

body.section: CO-1686 is a potent and irreversible inhibitor of EGFR in vitro
body.text: As expected for a first generation TKI, erlotinib potently inhibited WT EGFR (Ki = 0.40 ± 0.03 nM) while it had little activity against EGFR L858R/T790M kinase (Ki = 98.0 ± 8.1 nM).

body.section: CO-1686 is a potent and irreversible inhibitor of EGFR in vitro
body.text: CO-1686 also demonstrated a favorable selectivity profile when profiled against 434 kinases (SI Table 1A).

body.section: CO-1686 is a potent and irreversible inhibitor of EGFR in vitro
body.text: Twenty-three targets (representing 14 different kinases) were identified to be inhibited >50% at 0.1 μM CO-1686.

body.section: CO-1686 is a potent and irreversible inhibitor of EGFR in vitro
body.text: EGFR del19, T790M, L858R/T790M and L858R mutant kinases demonstrated the highest degree of inhibition, indicating the specificity of CO-1686, however, other kinase targets were observed to be inhibited at lower potency including FAK, CHK2, ERBB4 and JAK3.

body.section: CO-1686 is a potent and irreversible inhibitor of EGFR in vitro
body.text: Specificity was also examined by apparent IC50 determination in kinases known to possess a cysteine equivalent to C797 in EGFR (SI Table 1B).

body.section: CO-1686 is a potent and irreversible inhibitor of EGFR in vitro
body.text: In comparison to EGFR T790M, other C797-related kinases are observed to be inhibited by CO-1686 with an IC50 >6-fold including members of the Tec-family and JAK3.

body.section: CO-1686 is a potent and irreversible inhibitor of EGFR in vitro
body.text: In summary, CO-1686 is the first EGFR inhibitor in clinical development that is mutant-selective and inhibits T790M more potently than WT EGFR.

body.text: We examined the effect of CO-1686 against other EGFR mutations occasionally found in lung cancer, such as G719S, an exon 19 insertion mutant (ex19ins: I744-K745insKIPVAI), an exon 20 insertion (ex20ins: H773-V774HVdup), and L861Q in surrogate kinase assays.

body.section: CO-1686 demonstrates anti-tumor activity in NSCLC EGFR mutant xenograft models
body.text: Initial CO-1686 pharmacokinetics were evaluated in female NCRnu.nu mice (n=3/gp) following IV and oral delivery (SI Fig. 4A, B).

body.section: CO-1686 demonstrates anti-tumor activity in NSCLC EGFR mutant xenograft models
body.text: CO-1686 displayed high oral bioavailability (65%) and a relatively long half-life of 2.6 hours when dosed at 20 mg/kg.

body.section: CO-1686 demonstrates anti-tumor activity in NSCLC EGFR mutant xenograft models
body.text: Tumor-bearing mice were dosed orally once daily with CO-1686 as single agent and its effect on tumor growth was determined in several EGFR dependent xenograft models (Fig. 3A-C).

body.section: CO-1686 demonstrates anti-tumor activity in NSCLC EGFR mutant xenograft models
body.text: Continuous oral dosing of CO-1686 causes dose-dependent and significant tumor growth inhibition in all EGFR-mutant models examined.

body.section: CO-1686 demonstrates anti-tumor activity in NSCLC EGFR mutant xenograft models
body.text: At 100 mg/kg/day CO-1686 caused tumor regressions in two erlotinib-resistant models expressing the L858R/T790M EGFR mutation, the NCI-H1975 cell line xenograft (Fig. 3A) and the patient-derived lung tumor xenograft (PDX) LUM1868 (Fig. 3B), while erlotinib had no inhibitory effect on tumor growth (Fig. 3A, B).

body.section: CO-1686 demonstrates anti-tumor activity in NSCLC EGFR mutant xenograft models
body.text: The second generation EGFR TKI afatinib reduced tumor growth in NCI-H1975 EGFR T790M xenograft model (Fig. 3A) but to a lesser extent than observed with CO-1686 (P < 0.01).

body.section: CO-1686 demonstrates anti-tumor activity in NSCLC EGFR mutant xenograft models
body.text: Anti-tumor activity of CO-1686 in the HCC827 xenograft model that expresses the exon del19 activating EGFR mutation was comparable to erlotinib and afatinib (Fig. 3C).

body.section: CO-1686 demonstrates anti-tumor activity in NSCLC EGFR mutant xenograft models
body.text: Exploration of different oral dosing schedules demonstrated that in the NCI-H1975 model CO-1686 caused tumor regressions either given as 100 mg/kg once daily (QD) or as 50 mg/kg twice daily (BID), with no significant alterations in body weight with either dosing schedule (SI Fig. 5A, B).

body.section: CO-1686 demonstrates anti-tumor activity in NSCLC EGFR mutant xenograft models
body.text: However, the BID CO-1686 administration schedule was statistically superior to QD day 15 post-dosing (P < 0.01) and was therefore chosen as the optimal dosing regimen (SI Fig. 5A).

body.section: CO-1686 is WT EGFR sparing in vivo
body.text: To demonstrate the mutant selectivity and wild-type sparing properties of CO-1686 in vivo, CO-1686 potency was evaluated in the A431 xenograft model which has been previously shown to be dependent on WT EGFR for proliferation (, ).

body.section: CO-1686 is WT EGFR sparing in vivo
body.text: In this model CO-1686 dosed at 50 mg/kg BID was compared to erlotinib and afatinib at their respective highest tolerated dose in mice (75 mg/kg QD PO and 20 mg/kg QD intraperitoneally (IP), respectively).

body.section: CO-1686 is WT EGFR sparing in vivo
body.text: CO-1686 exhibited a minimal (36% TGI) although significant (P < 0.01) reduction in tumor growth, while both erlotinib and afatinib administration resulted in tumor regression (Fig. 3D).

body.section: CO-1686 is WT EGFR sparing in vivo
body.text: A431 tumor lysates from animals in each treatment group were analyzed for phosphorylated WT EGFR at tyrosine 1068 (a known marker for EGFR activation; Fig. 4A, B).

body.section: CO-1686 is WT EGFR sparing in vivo
body.text: Compared to the vehicle control group, A431 tumors harvested from animals treated with 50 mg/kg BID CO-1686 had no detectable reductions in EGFR phosphorylation (84% phosphorylated EGFR relative to vehicle; P = 0.58; Fig. 4B).

body.section: CO-1686 is WT EGFR sparing in vivo
body.text: In contrast, A431 tumors harvested from animals treated with 75 mg/kg QD erlotinib and 20 mg/kg QD afatinib had statistically significant reductions in EGFR phosphorylation (12% and 2% phosphorylated EGFR relative to vehicle, respectively; P < 0.05 in both cases; Fig. 4A, B).

body.section: CO-1686 is WT EGFR sparing in vivo
body.text: In addition, consistent with a lack of WT EGFR inhibition, CO-1686 administration did not cause significant mouse body weight changes in the A431 xenograft experiment (SI Fig. 6).

body.section: CO-1686 is WT EGFR sparing in vivo
body.text: Bodyweight loss was observed in both erlotinib and afatinib-treated groups (P < 0.01).

body.section: CO-1686 is WT EGFR sparing in vivo
body.text: Sparing of WT EGFR downstream signaling by CO-1686 was also examined in mouse skin (Fig. 4C).

body.section: CO-1686 is WT EGFR sparing in vivo
body.text: Administration of CO-1686 at the efficacious dose of 100 mg/kg QD for 5 days had no effect on phospho-MAPK levels in normal mouse skin, while erlotinib and afatinib both inhibited MAPK phosphorylation (Fig. 4C).

body.section: CO-1686 is WT EGFR sparing in vivo
body.text: These results demonstrate that CO-1686, contrary to first and second generation TKIs, spares WT EGFR in vivo at efficacious exposures that cause significant growth inhibition of tumors harboring mutant EGFR, including T790M.

body.text: Consistent with a mesenchymal cell signature in the COR clones, vimentin (VIM) expression was up-regulated and E-cadherin (CDH1) down-regulated in the CO-1686 resistant clones at the protein and RNA level. qRT-PCR analysis of additional markers further supported EMT including the up-regulation of AXL, ZEB1 CDH5, FN1 and the down-regulation of the epithelial markers MIR200B (), CLDN4, EPCAM and CLDN7.

body.text: EGFR expression was moderately reduced in the COR cell clones compared to the parental NCI-H1975 cell line; however, EGF ligand expression was induced as demonstrated by qRT-PCR (Fig. 5C).

body.section: Acquired resistance to CO-1686 is associated with EMT in T790M-positive NCI-H1975 cells
body.text: Amplification of the MET gene is observed in approximately 5-10% of NSCLC patients failing first generation EGFR TKIs (, ).

body.section: Acquired resistance to CO-1686 is associated with EMT in T790M-positive NCI-H1975 cells
body.text: An additional sub-population of EGFR TKI resistant patients also up-regulate the MET ligand, hepatocyte growth factor (HGF; ()).

body.section: Acquired resistance to CO-1686 is associated with EMT in T790M-positive NCI-H1975 cells
body.text: Analysis of phosphorylated MET in the COR clones indicated that the HGF pathway was not activated following CO-1686 resistance in the NCI-H1975 cell line (SI Fig. 10), and expression of the MET receptor was significantly reduced in the COR cell clones at the RNA level (Fig. 5C).

body.section: Acquired resistance to CO-1686 is associated with EMT in T790M-positive NCI-H1975 cells
body.text: ERBB2 amplification may be associated with acquired resistance especially in patients without detected T790M mutations (, ).

body.section: Acquired resistance to CO-1686 is associated with EMT in T790M-positive NCI-H1975 cells
body.text: Activation of additional EGFR receptor members ERBB2 and ERBB3 by phosphorylation was also not observed and actually appeared to be decreased in the COR clones compared to the parental NCI-H1975 cell line (Fig. 5C; SI Fig. 10).

body.section: CO-1686 resistant NSCLC cell lines are sensitive to AKT inhibition
body.text: We next examined potential druggable targets over-expressed in CO-1686 resistant cell clones that when inhibited could potentially restore CO-1686 sensitivity.

body.section: CO-1686 resistant NSCLC cell lines are sensitive to AKT inhibition
body.text: Higher basal levels of phosphorylated AKT (pAKT) were observed in the COR cell clones compared to the parental NCI-H1975 cell line (SI Fig.10).

body.section: CO-1686 resistant NSCLC cell lines are sensitive to AKT inhibition
body.text: Addition of CO-1686 resulted in the complete reduction of pAKT to negligible levels in the NCI-H1975 parental cell line (SI Fig. 10).

body.section: CO-1686 resistant NSCLC cell lines are sensitive to AKT inhibition
body.text: In comparison, CO-1686 addition to the COR cell clones, while reducing pAKT did not completely inhibit pAKT levels (SI Fig. 10).

body.section: CO-1686 resistant NSCLC cell lines are sensitive to AKT inhibition
body.text: Examining AKT isoform RNA expression in the COR cell clones by RNA-seq and qRT-PCR indicated that AKT3 expression was up-regulated 12- and 121-fold, respectively (P < 0.001; Fig. 5C).

body.section: CO-1686 resistant NSCLC cell lines are sensitive to AKT inhibition
body.text: Consistent with the RNA data, AKT3 was also up-regulated in the COR clones compared to the parental cell line at the protein level (SI Fig. 10).

body.section: CO-1686 resistant NSCLC cell lines are sensitive to AKT inhibition
body.text: AKT2 RNA was increased approximately 2-fold (P < 0.001) by RNA-Seq and qRT-PCR analysis (Fig. 5C).

body.section: CO-1686 resistant NSCLC cell lines are sensitive to AKT inhibition
body.text: No change was observed for AKT1 RNA expression (data not shown).

body.section: CO-1686 resistant NSCLC cell lines are sensitive to AKT inhibition
body.text: Given the up-regulation of AKT isoforms and continued AKT signaling in the presence of CO-1686 in the COR cell clones, we examined the impact of AKT inhibition on CO-1686 resistance using the AKT inhibitors MK-2206 () and GDC-0068 () that are currently in clinical development for multiple oncology indications.

body.section: CO-1686 resistant NSCLC cell lines are sensitive to AKT inhibition
body.text: Although not effective when used as a single agent (Fig. 5D), both MK-2206 and GDC-0068 restored partial drug sensitivity to the COR10-1 clone when used together in an equimolar fashion with CO-1686, with a combination index (CI) of 0.1, indicative of strong synergism.

body.section: CO-1686 resistant NSCLC cell lines are sensitive to AKT inhibition
body.text: Synergy between AKT inhibition and CO-1686 was also observed in additional COR cell clones (data not shown).

body.section: CO-1686 resistant NSCLC cell lines are sensitive to AKT inhibition
body.text: The up-regulation of AXL receptor tyrosine kinase has previously been reported in EGFR-resistant NSCLC (, ).

body.section: CO-1686 resistant NSCLC cell lines are sensitive to AKT inhibition
body.text: Consistent with these reports, AXL was observed to be up-regulated at the RNA (SI Table 2; Fig. 5C) and protein level (SI Fig. 10) in the CO-1686 resistant COR cell clones compared to the parental cell line.

body.section: CO-1686 resistant NSCLC cell lines are sensitive to AKT inhibition
body.text: In addition, growth arrest-specific 6 (Gas6), a ligand of AXL implicated in EGFR TKI resistance (, ) was significantly up-regulated in COR cell clones as determined by RNA-Seq and qRT-PCR analysis (Fig. 5C).

body.section: CO-1686 resistant NSCLC cell lines are sensitive to AKT inhibition
body.text: AXL kinase function was inhibited employing XL-880, a VEGFR/MET/AXL inhibitor (Foretinib; Exelixis ()).

body.section: CO-1686 resistant NSCLC cell lines are sensitive to AKT inhibition
body.text: Pharmacological inhibition of AXL kinase activity restored partial sensitivity of EGFR TKI resistant COR cell clones to CO-1686 (SI Fig. 11A), however, this effect was modest in comparison to previous reports () with a CI of 0.53 and 0.44 for COR1-1 and COR10-1, respectively, indicative of synergy.

body.section: CO-1686 resistant NSCLC cell lines are sensitive to AKT inhibition
body.text: Combination of CO-1686 with R428, an AXL-selective small molecule inhibitor () produced comparable results to XL-880 (data not shown).

body.section: CO-1686 resistant NSCLC cell lines are sensitive to AKT inhibition
body.text: Given the multiple targets inhibited by small molecule kinase inhibitors, the role of AXL inhibition in sensitizing COR cell clones to CO-1686 was specifically examined using siRNA to knockdown AXL expression (SI Fig.11B, C).

body.section: CO-1686 resistant NSCLC cell lines are sensitive to AKT inhibition
body.text: Despite effective AXL knockdown at the mRNA and protein level (SI Fig. 11B) only a modest reduction in CO-1686 GI50 in the COR1-1 and COR10-1 clones of 2.2 and 1.6-fold, respectively (SI Fig. 11C), was observed.

body.section: CO-1686 resistant NSCLC cell lines are sensitive to AKT inhibition
body.text: In addition, we generated stable pools of parental NCI-H1975 cells that over-expressed AXL at the mRNA and protein level (SI Fig. 11D) and determined the GI50 for CO-1686.

body.section: CO-1686 resistant NSCLC cell lines are sensitive to AKT inhibition
body.text: Compared to the parental cell line, NCI-H1975 cell populations over-expressing AXL had a slight increase in CO-1686 GI50 of approximately 2-fold (SI Fig. 11E).

body.section: CO-1686 resistant NSCLC cell lines are sensitive to AKT inhibition
body.text: To place this result into perspective, the CO-1686 GI50 of the COR cell clones 1-1 and 10-1 that over-express AXL ~100-fold over the parental NCI-H1975 cell line (Fig. 5C) are > 1000nM and the NCI-H1975 cell line engineered to over-express AXL at 195-fold above the parental cell line is 52 nM.

body.section: CO-1686 resistant NSCLC cell lines are sensitive to AKT inhibition
body.text: Therefore, in our studies, although small molecule inhibitors of AXL kinase can partially restore the sensitivity of COR cell lines to CO-1686, the specific role of AXL inhibition in this effect appears minimal and perhaps related the broader spectrum of kinases inhibited by these agents.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: T790M-driven lung cancer is a growing clinical problem given widespread screening of lung adenocarcinoma patients for activating EGFR mutations and consequent recommended use of erlotinib or gefitinib as front-line therapy in EGFRmut patients (NCCN guidelines version 2.2013 non-small cell lung cancer).

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Significantly, early clinical evidence suggests that a secondary T790M mutation can drive resistance to second generation TKIs such as afatinib as well ().

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: CO-1686 has attractive relevant properties as a potential therapeutic for T790M positive EGFRmut NSCLC.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: It potently inhibits the kinase activity of EGFR carrying the T790M mutation, both in vitro and after oral administration in vivo (cell line xenograft and patient-derived xenograft).

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: This inhibitory activity against a pathogenic mutant form of EGFR is not accompanied by meaningful wild-type EGFR inhibition, suggesting that drug tolerability may be superior to first and second generation TKIs, for which key toxicities of skin rash, diarrhea and interstitial lung disease are attributed to wild-type EGFR inhibition (, ).

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: CO-1686 is currently in a human dose-escalation study to evaluate safety, pharmacokinetics, and preliminary efficacy in previously treated EGFRmut NSCLC patients (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT01526928).

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Although still in dose-escalation phase and the maximal tolerated dose not reached, objective RECIST responses have been observed in heavily pretreated T790M positive NSCLC patients administered CO-1686 following the development of resistance to erlotinib ().

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Additionally, metastasis shrinkage has been observed at multiple organ sites, including both brain and liver metastases.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Consistent with the preclinical data presented in this paper, CO-1686 appears to be well-tolerated with no evidence of dose-related diarrhea or rash.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: CO-1686 potently inhibits single activating mutant forms of EGFR, both in vitro and in vivo (cell line xenograft and human EGFR transgenic mouse models).

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Assuming that this non-clinical activity translates into clinical efficacy in treatment naïve EGFRmut patients, an interesting question is whether the development of acquired resistance to CO-1686 will be slower than acquisition of resistance to first generation TKIs, such that progression-free survival with CO-1686 would be superior to erlotinib.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Initial studies of in vitro resistance to CO-1686 demonstrate enrichment of an RNA-based signature associated with EMT.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: A similar signature has been observed in cell lines resistant to EGFR and PI3K/Akt inhibitors ().

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: In support of the CO-1686 resistance data performed in the NCI-H1975 cell background, we have also generated CO-1686 resistant clones of the HCC827 cell line (EGFR del19).

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: EMT is also associated with resistance in these cell clones, with the down-regulation of E-cadherin and up-regulation of vimentin at the RNA and protein level (data not shown).

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: In addition, recent work from two independent investigators using a tool-compound structurally related to CO-1686, termed CNX-2006 (Celgene), also indicated that EMT is associated with resistance in multiple cell backgrounds (, ).

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Recent papers indicate that resistance to WZ4002, a covalent EGFR inhibitor, is mediated by IGF1R pathway activation due to the repression of IGFBP3 expression via promoter methylation () or genomic amplification of the MAPK1 (ERK2) gene ().

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: These specific mechanisms were not observed in our studies (data not shown).

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Two key next steps with CO-1686 are (a) to assess the kinetics of acquired EMT and compare with acquired T790M using in vitro and in vivo systems, and (b) to examine the value of combinatorial therapy targeting the specific resistance pathways defined above.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: It is encouraging that resistance to CO-1686 has not yet been observed to be driven by direct EGFR pathway modification.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: This suggests that CO-1686 may be sufficient to functionally silence mutant EGFR signaling at clinically achievable concentrations, a key therapeutic goal in EGFRmut NSCLC that has not been achieved with the currently available clinical TKIs due to acquired resistance within the pathway that leads to patient relapse.

body.section: DISCUSSION
body.text: Moreover, the sparing of wild-type EGFR by CO-1686 may allow for evaluation of combination therapies with less potential for overlapping toxicities in patients.
